feed.title: Combined summary - PQC output type discussion

entry.title: Combined summary - PQC output type discussion
entry.summary: The recent email discussions have been pivotal in addressing the imminent quantum computing threats to Bitcoin, with a primary focus on integrating advanced cryptographic measures to enhance its security. The proposed integration of a P2TRv2 output type is designed to facilitate emergency post-quantum cryptography (PQC) by incorporating features such as Tripwire and Miner Lockdown. These features aim to maintain economic feasibility by keeping fee structures close to current models and simplifying the transition for developers and users alike. This approach is crucial in addressing the "steal-or-freeze" dilemma which threatens Bitcoin's core value proposition. Additionally, a more comprehensive, yet complex strategy involving a P2MR-based output type is discussed. This setup includes new witness styles essential for a complete shift following the emergence of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer (CRQC), although it could lead to slower adoption due to its intricate requirements. Further insights from the discussion highlight various innovative transaction output types being considered to bolster Bitcoin against quantum vulnerabilities. Among these, the Pay to Merkle Root (P2MR) and Pay to Quantum Resistant (P2QR) models stand out. Specifically, P2MR allows the transaction output to store a Merkle root representing a tree of leaf scripts, which keeps EC points off-chain until necessary. This model is analyzed in [BIP 360](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/8c369ac8e60629ac6c032ffe21bb5ec5b35213d7/bip-0360.mediawiki). On the other hand, P2QR starts by disabling ECC opcodes to ensure quantum resistance from the onset. The P2TRv2 model, detailed in [BIP 341](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/9783d61f1b9c81231581fee026c8e8cb9499d265/bip-0341.mediawiki), introduces PQC opcodes and plans for a future consensus change to disable ECC within the output type itself, offering a balanced approach. A practical application of these theoretical models is demonstrated through the implementation of BIP-360 P2MR in Bitcoin Core on regtest, found [here](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/bip-360-p2mr-implemented-in-bitcoin-core-on-regtest-vector-results-measurements-spec-feedback). This implementation provides concrete data on transaction efficiency, showing that P2MR can be more efficient than traditional script paths under certain configurations. The results underline the potential for real-world application and scalability of these new cryptographic frameworks. Proposals for new witness styles and modifications to the P2P protocol are also discussed, aiming to facilitate the deployment of these transaction output changes. Elements like Public Key Recovery (PKR) are suggested to reduce exposure of public keys at spending time, which could save space and enhance security by recovering the public key using a signature against the public key hash. Moreover, security strategies like Tripwire and Miner Lockdown are considered to provide mechanisms to disable ECC under specific conditions, thus safeguarding against unexpected vulnerabilities. These discussions reflect a proactive community effort to prepare Bitcoin for quantum threats by exploring various paths that balance security, efficiency, and backward compatibility.
